chunks.heading: What makes a metal "reactive"?
chunks.body: Metals react by losing electrons. The easier a metal loses its electrons, the more reactive it is.
chunks.checkText: A highly reactive metal is one that loses electrons...

chunks.heading: Displacement reactions
chunks.body: A more [[chem-reactivity-of-metals|reactive]] metal can push a less reactive metal out of a compound. It takes that metal's place, leaving the less reactive one free.
chunks.checkText: In a displacement reaction, which metal ends up free?

chunks.heading: Why reactions need collisions
chunks.body: For a reaction to happen, particles must collide with enough energy. Anything that causes more of these collisions speeds the reaction up.

chunks.heading: Concentration and reaction rate
chunks.body: A higher concentration packs more particles into the same space. That means more [[chem-collision-theory|collisions]], so the reaction goes faster.
chunks.checkText: Raising concentration speeds up a reaction because it causes...

chunks.heading: Temperature and reaction rate
chunks.body: Heat makes particles move faster. Faster particles [[chem-collision-theory|collide]] more often and harder, so the reaction speeds up.
chunks.checkText: Raising temperature speeds up a reaction mainly because particles...

chunks.heading: Surface area and reaction rate
chunks.body: Crushing a solid into powder exposes far more surface. More exposed surface means more chances to [[chem-collision-theory|collide]], so the reaction speeds up.
chunks.checkText: Powder reacts faster than a solid lump mainly because it has more...

chunks.heading: Catalysts — a shortcut, not a cheat
chunks.body: A catalyst gives a reaction an easier path that needs less energy to start. It comes out the other end unchanged, ready to be used again.
chunks.checkText: Does a catalyst get used up in a reaction?

chunks.heading: Energy in and energy out
chunks.body: An exothermic reaction releases heat to its surroundings. An endothermic reaction absorbs heat instead.
chunks.checkText: A reaction that releases heat to its surroundings is called...

chunks.heading: Hess's Law, the short version
chunks.body: Hess's Law says a reaction's total energy change depends only on where you start and end — not on the path taken to get there.
chunks.checkText: Hess's Law says a reaction's energy change depends on...
